title: Bouar megaliths erected
description: Stones tonnes in weight are set up in groups over a wide area west of Bouar, the oldest monuments known in the region.

title: Bangui founded
description: Albert Dolisie builds a French post at the head of navigation on the Ubangi River, which grows into the capital.

title: Ubangi-Shari territory created
description: The French conquest between the Ubangi and the Chari is organised as a separate territory, from 1910 part of French Equatorial Africa.

title: Kongo-Wara rebellion
description: The healer-chief Karnu's movement of Gbaya and others fights the colony's forced labour for three years before it is crushed, one of the largest revolts in French Equatorial Africa.

title: Ubangi-Shari rallies to Free France
description: After Chad, the administration at Bangui declares for de Gaulle, making French Equatorial Africa the first colonial bloc on the Free French side.

title: Boganda founds MESAN
description: Barthélemy Boganda, Catholic priest turned deputy in Paris, founds the Movement for the Social Evolution of Black Africa with the slogan 'zo kwe zo', every person is a person.

title: Central African Republic proclaimed
description: Boganda proclaims the Central African Republic an autonomous state of the French Community.

title: Boganda dies in an air crash
description: The republic's founder dies when his plane explodes in flight, a year before the independence he had negotiated is proclaimed.

title: Independence from France
description: The Central African Republic becomes fully independent, with David Dacko its first president.

title: Bokassa seizes power
description: Army chief Jean-Bédel Bokassa overthrows President Dacko, his cousin, in the Saint-Sylvestre coup and jails him.

title: Central African Empire proclaimed
description: Bokassa renames the republic an empire and himself Emperor Bokassa I.

title: Coronation of Bokassa I
description: The emperor crowns himself in a ceremony modelled on Napoleon's that swallows a quarter of the year's budget and draws the world's ridicule.

title: Schoolchildren massacred
description: Around a hundred pupils arrested after protests against compulsory school uniforms die in prison, the scandal that dooms the empire.

title: Operation Barracuda ends the empire
description: French paratroopers fly in unopposed while Bokassa is abroad and restore David Dacko as president of a reborn republic.

title: Kolingba coup
description: General André Kolingba overthrows Dacko after a disputed election and imposes military rule for a decade.

title: Patassé wins free elections
description: Ange-Félix Patassé wins the presidency, but unpaid soldiers mutiny again and again in the years that follow.

title: Bozizé takes Bangui
description: François Bozizé seizes the capital while Patassé is abroad and rules for the next decade.

title: Séléka takes Bangui
description: The mostly Muslim Séléka coalition storms the capital and makes Michel Djotodia president; looting and retaliation against Christians spiral into civil war.

title: UN peacekeepers deploy
description: The UN mission MINUSCA takes over from African and French forces as sectarian killing empties whole districts.

title: Touadéra elected president
description: Faustin-Archange Touadéra, a former prime minister and mathematics professor, wins the run-off that ends the transition.
